entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Titus Quinctius Flamininus was a Roman politician and general instrumental in the Roman conquest of Greece.

Born into a family of prominent Roman senators, Flamininus would eventually rise to become consul in 173 BCE, a position he held alongside Gaius Claudius Pulcher.

As a skilled military commander, Flamininus led the Roman legions to victory in the Second Macedonian War, forcing the kingdom of Macedon to submit to Roman authority and paying a significant indemnity to Rome. This marked a turning point in Roman expansion into Greece, solidifying Roman control over the region and paving the way for the eventual rise of the Roman Empire.

The legacy of Titus Quinctius Flamininus can be seen in the Roman Empire's continued expansion into Greece and the subsequent establishment of Roman governance in the region.

"The Greeks are not so much conquered, as they have been civilized." - Titus Quinctius Flamininus
